title: Cyclotomic projective covers and dualities descend through the quotient
statement: Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient. For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$, $B\otimes_A P(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom duality commutes with this basechange, and finite vector duality commutes with inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_B S)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise is used.
strategy:
Tensor a shifted-free retract to prove finite projectivity. Every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes P$ lifts through $P\to B\otimes P$ by generic projectivity; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so this is a surjective endomorphism-ring homomorphism. Its domain is local for indecomposable $P$, hence a nonzero quotient is indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential: pull back a submodule and use the old superfluous kernel. If $JS\ne0$ and $P/JP\ne0$, finite dimension supplies a simple quotient, which must be the old unique head $S$, contradicting its being annihilated by $J$. Every $B$-simple inflates to a generic simple; its descended cover therefore exhausts the projective basis, proving surjectivity and no merging.
For finite $P$, evaluation on a shifted-free module and restriction to retracts gives $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes P,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_A B$. Applying $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes P)^\#=B\otimes P^\#$. Inflation does not change $D_\psi S$. Use only the choice-free finite-module normalization clauses of the generic positive-divided-string supplier. They yield the unique self-dual representatives; no conditional quantum-global clause is used.
Finally $h(P,S)=T(P^\#,S)$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ by evaluation of a tensor functional. A normalized cover has $h(P,S)=q^a$ because absolute $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$. Both dualities fix the normalized labels, so $q^a=q^{-a}$ and $a=0$. Other simple heads have zero Hom. Shift-orbit bases now make both normalized pairings perfect. This proof distinguishes projective Hom duality from vector duality and never uses a symmetric trace.

title: Normalized cyclotomic functors give an integrable quantum action
statement: For the standard graded quotient over arbitrary $k$ and graded admissible $Q$, let $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. On projective $K_0$ take $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta+i$ to output $\beta$. On module $G_0$ take the KK action $E_i=E_i^{\rm basic}$ and $F_i=q_i^{1-h}F_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta$; also the canonical action with the SAME shifts as projectives. The torus acts on root component $\beta$ by $K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$. Each action satisfies all mixed relations, and $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent. After scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$ these are integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules. This does not assert a decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules and does not cover ungraded monic deformations.
strategy:
Projectivity supplies exact functors and preservation of finite projectives, so the displayed shifts give $A$-linear operators. In the basic commutator at target $\beta$, multiply $EF$ by $q_i^{1-h}$; the $q_i^{-2}FE$ term becomes precisely the normalized $FE$ at its changed target, and identity terms become $\sum_{k=0}^{h-1}q_i^{1-h+2k}=[h]_i$. The negative case gives the signed counterpart. In the KK representation action the same factors are instead carried by $F$; in the canonical representation action they are carried by $E$, so the same computation holds. Unequal-color basic crossing shift $q^{-b_{ij}}$ cancels the change of the normalizing $h_i$ under removing/adding $j$.
Restriction lowers height. The dot/root-string lemma gives $R^\Lambda(\beta+ni)=0$ for large $n$, so induction is locally nilpotent componentwise. Every Grothendieck element has finite root support and the displayed torus labels are correct. The general mixed/local-nilpotence lemma proves BOTH full symmetrizable Serre families by finite rank-one Hom adjoint modules, giving the unique rational quantum action without an A2 or rank-two local-finiteness assumption. All these steps precede vacuum generation and the integral highest-module identification, so no cyclic dependency is used.
